title: POC Weekly - Caching Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on prefix/KV cache hit rates and prompt reuse strategy. Reviewed latest metrics, identified key causes for cache misses (prompt variance, short TTLs, partial key mismatches), discussed warm-up strategy and traffic shaping, agreed on experiments to increase prefix reuse and KV cache effectiveness. Next steps include running expanded benchmark, sharing updated dashboard, and a deeper technical deep-dive on cache eviction and quantization impact.
next_steps: Samir to share updated cache-hit dashboard and raw logs by 2025-03-27
BrightCart to provide sample 2k anonymized prompts for reuse analysis by 2025-03-28
Jordan to send pricing impact estimate for higher cache tiers by 2025-03-30
Schedule deep-dive on eviction policies and quantization with BrightCart engineers (target week of 2025-04-07)
action_items: Samir Patel: run 100k request benchmark with 30% repeated-prefix traffic and share results (due 2025-03-27)
Emily Chen: export 2k representative prompts (anonymized) and share in secure link (due 2025-03-28)
Liam O'Connor: instrument KV cache metrics on staging (hit/miss by prefix/hash) and confirm labels (due 2025-03-26)
Jordan Lee: send short pricing note for Dedicated cache tier and cost/cpu tradeoffs (due 2025-03-30)
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2025-03-25 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Emily Chen (BrightCart SRE), Liam O'Connor (BrightCart ML Eng), Aisha Malik (BrightCart PM)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for making time today, quick agenda — hit rates, prompt reuse, warm-up, next steps. Samir will run through the numbers.
[00:18] Samir: ok so quick snapshot from the last 48 hours on staging: overall prefix cache hit rate is about 23% initially, but when we fold in prompt-template normalization we see effective reuse up to ~67% for the top 10 flows. KV cache hit rate on model side is at 41% average, but that varies a lot by endpoint.
[00:37] Emily: whoa 23% to 67% — that gap seems big, is the normalization just folding similar prompts or are we changing semantics?
[00:45] Samir: mostly normalization — we strip user IDs, reorder some attributes, and canonicalize date formats. We also bucket some optional fields. so semantically equivalent prompts align. There's a small risk of over-normalizing but we haven't seen quality regression in the eval set.
[01:05] Liam: the KV numbers — 41% — do those include cold starts? we saw really low hits after deploys.
[01:12] Samir: good point; the 41% is across the board including cold windows. If you exclude cold start windows (first 30 minutes post-deploy), hit climbs to 56%. The warm-up strategy matters a lot.
[01:28] Aisha: can you explain cold windows — like why are we missing so much after deploys?
[01:33] Samir: two reasons: 1) the KV cache is mounted per-runtime instance and when new pods spin up the instance-level cache is empty; 2) our current TTLs are short (~10m) so infrequent prefixes expire quickly and we don't retain them across bursts. Also small mismatch in prefix key formation — sometimes we include trailing whitespace or extra punctuation so keys don't match.
[01:55] Jordan: transcription note — sometimes fireflies messes up K-V as K-V cash but you get the idea.
[02:02] Emily: yes no worries. So what's your recommendation? longer TTLs? centralized KV store?
[02:09] Samir: a few levers: extend TTLs for hot prefixes, use a shared KV backend for cross-instance hits (costly but effective), and improve canonicalization of prefixes — small templating changes can boost reuse. Also consider aggressive warm-up after deploys: synthetic hits that prime hot keys.
[02:32] Liam: what's the cost tradeoff for a shared KV backend? network latency?
[02:36] Samir: there's some added network egress and a few ms latency per token if we consult an external KV for every request. But we can do a hybrid: local LRU cache plus a background async heater that populates local caches from central KV for hot keys. That keeps tail latency low.
[02:55] Emily: do we have numbers on tail latency when local cache misses and we go to central?
[03:00] Samir: on our test cluster we saw p95 increase of ~12-18ms when falling back to central KV, p99s were higher by ~40ms in worst cases. But most interestingly, if hits go from 40% to 70% the overall token cost drops ~22% in our sim, because fewer model token regen calls are needed.
[03:24] Aisha: ok so more cost in central KV but net token cost savings — makes sense. How about prompt changes — what exactly did you do to get to 67%?
[03:33] Samir: we refactored prompts into a small set of canonical templates. For user-specific content we replaced fattail fields with stable placeholders, and we added a short hashing step for long free-text fields so that semantically same free text maps to the same key when within a similarity threshold. It's imperfect but it bumped reuse a lot.
[03:54] Liam: hashing free-text — do you have false positive risk where different texts hash to same bucket?
[03:59] Samir: we use a sharded sim-hash with a high threshold; false positives are rare and we validated against a small human eval set. When unsure we fall back to model.
[04:12] Jordan: any customer-visible regressions?
[04:14] Samir: none observed in our staging evals. We have a few edge cases where dates in natural language got canonicalized incorrectly — we flagged those and will tweak the parser.
[04:25] Emily: benchmarks — you mentioned synthetic warm-up; how do we measure effectiveness?
[04:29] Samir: we run a 100k request workload with a defined repetition ratio (we used 30% repeated prefixes in our sim). With that config warm-up delivered a 34% higher hit rate in the first 10 minutes and cut model token calls significantly.
[04:46] Emily: can you share the raw logs? we'd like to see distribution by prefix.
[04:49] Samir: yes will share; I'll post the dashboard with per-prefix hits, TTL evictions, and per-instance stats.
[04:57] Liam: quick question on batching interplay — if we increase batching, do we lose opportunity for prefix cache hits because requests are combined differently?
[05:03] Samir: batching shouldn't change prefix keys; however batching can reorder micro-timings so cache warm-up patterns change. We saw negligible negative impact in our tests, but it depends on how you parallelize. Batching can help cost a lot though so we want both.
[05:20] Aisha: any concerns about security/compliance with central KV? BrightCart needs audit logs and KMS.
[05:26] Samir: absolutely — central KV integrates with KMS/HSM and we can enable per-request audit logging and RBAC. For private deployments we can keep the KV inside the VPC and use customer keys.
[05:39] Emily: good. On the dashboard, can we get a view that ties hit-rate regressions to deploys and to specific template versions?
[05:46] Samir: yes we'll add annotations for deploys and template hash versions. That helps root-cause.
[05:52] Jordan: let's talk about experiments — priority 1 is get staging benchmark with the new canonicalization and warm-up, priority 2 is central KV proof-of-concept on a small pool, priority 3 is prompt template cleanup by BrightCart.
[06:05] Emily: timeline?
[06:07] Jordan: Samir thinks he can run and share the benchmark by Thursday (2025-03-27). BrightCart will send anonymized prompts by Friday (2025-03-28). Pricing note from me by Monday (2025-03-30).
[06:18] Liam: small nit — we saw some mis-keys because of unicode normalization, e.g. non-breaking space in product titles. Can you normalize unicode?
[06:26] Samir: yes we'll add unicode NFC normalization in the pipeline. That should fix a chunk of misses.
[06:31] Aisha: will this affect evals? want to make sure our A/B metrics are stable.
[06:35] Samir: we'll run A/B on a shadow traffic slice first. No live change until we validate.
[06:40] Jordan: any blockers?
[06:42] Emily: main blocker is getting the sample prompts. Also need to validate that the anonymization process stays within our privacy policy.
[06:49] Jordan: totally — we'll accept a hashed or partially redacted export. Samir will provide guidance on formatting.
[06:55] Samir: note on eviction: current LRU window combined with short TTLs means a hot key can be evicted during sudden bursts. We'll propose a small change: pin top N keys per instance for X minutes (configurable) to avoid thrash.
[07:12] Liam: pinning top keys per instance sounds good but watch memory footprint.
[07:16] Samir: yes we'll simulate memory impact. It's configurable per-pod.
[07:21] Jordan: ok let's recap action items.
[07:24] Samir: I'll run the 100k benchmark and share the dashboard (due 2025-03-27). I'll also add deploy and template annotations to the dashboard.
[07:33] Emily: BrightCart will export 2k prompts anonymized (due 2025-03-28). Liam will instrument additional KV metrics (due 2025-03-26).
[07:41] Jordan: I'll send pricing / Dedicated cache tier note (due 2025-03-30). We'll schedule a deep-dive for first week of April on eviction and quantization impact.
[07:51] Aisha: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[07:54] Jordan: thanks — we’ll follow up in email with links.
[07:58] (end)
questions: What is the best warm-up strategy to reduce cold-start misses?
How much does central KV increase p95/p99 latency in practice?
Can prompt canonicalization be done without quality regressions?
